data.narrative:
Cognition, a Series A AI & Software company founded by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan, has raised $400M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private firms and 1 public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) operating in AI and software infrastructure.

Two triangulation methods anchor this analysis. Stage-progression methodology, using total raised as a proxy base of $5M and applying a 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implies a $9M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B, Series B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B, Series B), and Field AI ($2.0B, Series B). The median across these four peers is $4.4B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $25.0B.

The triangulated analysis produces a valuation range of $8M (low) to $5.1B (high), with a median of $2.2B. The substantial spread reflects material uncertainty: the stage-progression method yields a materially lower result ($9M) than peer-median ($4.4B), suggesting either that comps command valuations well above typical Series A multiples or that Cognition's funding scale and/or traction position it distinctly within the peer set. Key uncertainties include product-market fit evidence, revenue run-rate, and whether Reflection AI's $25B valuation represents an outlier or signals market appetite for frontier AI software companies at this stage.
